subject: Social Habits
title: Calming big feelings
objectives: Children will notice big feelings in their bodies.
Children will use slow breathing or a calm place with an adult.
content: Big feelings in my body, breathing and calming, and asking for help.
teachingActivities: Stay calm yourself; name the feeling first ("You are cross"); never punish a child for a big feeling; offer a calm corner as a safe place, not a punishment; teach slow breathing with a pinwheel or a teddy; use a feelings chart; teach asking for help in words or a gesture.
learnerActivities: Notice big feelings in the body, use slow breathing with an adult and ask for help when upset.
assessment: Observe whether each child uses a calming strategy with adult support and asks for help.
expectedOutcomes: Uses a calming strategy with adult support.
Asks an adult for help when upset.

lessons.title: Big feelings in my body
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will notice where big feelings are in their bodies.
successCriteria: Points to where a feeling is in the body
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name feelings and try new things.
lessons.starter: Say "When I am cross, my face is hot and my fists are tight. Show me."
teacherActivities: Show how a cross body looks: tight fists, hot face.
Show how a calm body looks: loose hands and soft face.
Ask "Where do you feel it?" and point to the body picture.
Say "All feelings are okay. We can calm down."
learnerActivities: Child points to a body part.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how a cross body looks: tight fists, hot face. Children: Children copy the body shape.
Step 2. Teacher: Show how a calm body looks: loose hands and soft face. Children: Children copy the calm body.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Where do you feel it?" and point to the body picture. Children: Child points to a body part.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "All feelings are okay. We can calm down." Children: Children repeat calm down.

practical.title: Body feelings
steps: Point to where you feel it.
practical.safety: Keep the movements gentle and never push a child to show strong feelings. Stop if a child becomes upset and comfort them.

differentiation.support: Show the body shape and copy together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what makes them feel cross.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How does a cross body look?
How does a calm body look?

expectedOutcomes: Notices big feelings in the body
lessons.conclusion: Take a calm body pose and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Name your child’s feelings and where you see them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "notice where big feelings are in their bodies" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: When I feel cross I stop and breathe.

lessons.title: Breathing and calming
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will use slow breathing to calm down.
successCriteria: Takes slow breaths with an adult
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name feelings and try new things.
lessons.starter: Hold a feather and say "Blow slowly and the feather floats."
teacherActivities: Show how to breathe in through the nose and out slowly like blowing a feather.
Let children blow a pinwheel slowly.
Place a teddy on the tummy and watch it rise and fall.
Say "Breathe in, breathe out. I am calm."
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to breathe in through the nose and out slowly like blowing a feather. Children: Children copy slowly.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children blow a pinwheel slowly. Children: Child blows the pinwheel gently.
Step 3. Teacher: Place a teddy on the tummy and watch it rise and fall. Children: Child breathes with the teddy.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Breathe in, breathe out. I am calm." Children: Children repeat calm.

practical.title: Teddy breathing
steps: Put a teddy on your tummy.
practical.safety: Offer a seat if lying down is not comfortable and keep each breath gentle. Never ask children to hold their breath.

differentiation.support: Breathe beside the child and count slowly.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to teach a friend to breathe slowly.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How do we breathe to calm?

lessons.conclusion: Take one more slow breath together.
lessons.homeConnection: Practise slow breathing with your child at bedtime.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use slow breathing to calm down" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Asking for help
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will ask an adult for help when they feel upset.
successCriteria: Says help or points to an adult
Goes to a calm corner with an adult
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name feelings and try new things.
lessons.starter: Show a puppet that is upset and say "The puppet is upset. It says: help please."
teacherActivities: Show the puppet asking a grown-up for help.
Show the calm corner and say "You can sit here with a grown-up."
Let children practise handing the help card to an adult.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the puppet asking a grown-up for help. Children: Children watch and say help.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the calm corner and say "You can sit here with a grown-up." Children: Children look at the corner.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children practise handing the help card to an adult. Children: Child gives the card.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Asking for help is brave." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Help card
steps: Give the help card to the teacher.
practical.safety: Keep the calm corner a safe, warm place and never use it as punishment. Stay with the child at all times.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to remind a friend to ask for help.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Uses the calm corner with an adult
lessons.homeConnection: Set up a calm place at home and visit it together.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "ask an adult for help when they feel upset" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: My calm plan
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will choose a calming strategy and use it in a pretend upset.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name feelings and try new things.
resources: Calming picture cards: breathe, hug a teddy, go to the corner, ask for help
lessons.starter: Show four calming cards and say "When we are upset, we choose one."
teacherActivities: Show each card and act it out.
Let the puppet feel cross and ask a child to choose a card.
Act out using the chosen idea.
learnerActivities: Children say I can calm down.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each card and act it out. Children: Children copy each action.
Step 2. Teacher: Let the puppet feel cross and ask a child to choose a card. Children: Child chooses a card.
Step 3. Teacher: Act out using the chosen idea. Children: Child acts out the idea.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "I can calm down." Children: Children say I can calm down.

practical.title: Calm cards
steps: Act it out with the puppet.
practical.safety: Keep the scene make-believe with the puppet. Stop if a child becomes distressed and comfort them.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to teach the puppet a calming idea.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What can we do to calm?

lessons.conclusion: Pick one calming idea and do it together.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a calm card set for home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "choose a calming strategy and use it in a pretend upset" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?

lessons.title: Week 2 calm check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child manages big feelings.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name feelings and try new things.
lessons.starter: Sing the calm song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: breathing, calm corner and cards.
At each station watch how the child responds.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: breathing, calm corner and cards. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child responds. Children: Child responds with a prompt.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Calm stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station closely and keep the mood quiet and kind. Stop any activity that upsets a child.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to guide a friend to the calm corner.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: notices big feelings; uses slow breathing; asks for help; uses the calm corner.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 2
lessons.conclusion: Take a slow breath and wave goodbye.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child manages big feelings" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
